correctness.rationale: Lyndon proper-suffix comparison yields disjoint contributions from one-, two-, three-marker factors; the sole zero-free exception is handled. Six exhaustive order chambers reduce the full distribution to seven rational geometric terms. Weak composition to Dirichlet convergence and exact component-moment calculations prove the nondegenerate limit. Standalone checks independently enumerated 7,315 words through length 21 and checked generating-function coefficients through length 70; finite checks supplement, not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2012 Lyndon/Fibonacci text treats lower bounds for Lyndon words and infinite-word complexity; the inspected 2017 Counting Lyndon Factors article treats unrestricted maximal distinct-factor counts and full-alphabet averages. Neither establishes the exact distribution at fixed binary weight three or the resulting Dirichlet mixture. The proposed new statements are not implied by these published maxima or unconditional expectations without an additional restricted-composition classification. Public and mathematical-record searches for weight-three, fixed Parikh vector, rational bivariate enumeration and aliases found no decisive covering result; unindexed equivalences remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The complete fixed-composition distribution is a natural structural refinement of unrestricted Lyndon-factor complexity, not another maximal bound. The nontrivial strict-gap indicator is required for exact counts; the rational bivariate series gives all finite spectra, and the Dirichlet mixture and positive limiting variance quantify characteristic fluctuations of sparse-marker words. This is a motivated complete infinite family, rather than an arbitrary single length or routine table recomputation.
